Жак (Хаим-Яков) Липшиц родился в Друскин: Jacques (Chaim Jacob) Lipchitz was born in Druskininkai in 1891 into a Jewish family — a Litvak, as Lithuanian Jews are called. His father, a building contractor, opened the “Central” hotel here in 1909. As a young man, Lipchitz left for Paris, became one of the founders of Cubism in sculpture, and was friends with Modigliani and Picasso. In 1941 he escaped from the Nazis to America, and in 1954 the Museum of Modern Art in New York held a large exhibition of his work. The museum tells the story of the sculptor and of the resort town's Jewish community.
